correctness.rationale: A unique leftmost embedding gives a bijection between distinct admissible source words and uniquely decomposed skipped blocks. Prefix, unequal-gap, equal-gap and suffix factors are independently proved as (1+z)/(1-(q-2)z), 1/(1-(q-2)z), (q-1)z/(1-(q-2)z), and 1/(1-(q-1)z). Their product establishes every coefficient for all q>=3,m>=1,d>=0. A positive coefficient recurrence proves exact strict ordering and absence of singleton parents at positive deletion count. Binomial transition counting and the binomial CLT prove multiplicity and asymptotic claims. Executable exhaustive and independent DP checks pass; finite checks are auxiliary, not infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: The checked primary texts supply unrestricted supersequence enumeration, binary run-limited one-error code constructions, and q-ary homopolymer-free Hamming bounds, but no statement covering all deletion radii and the complete inverse-list distribution for q-ary adjacency-distinct sources. Semantic literature searches surfaced different objects (deleted overlapping reads, unconstrained source-to-output deletion spheres, scattered-subsequence universality); these do not imply the restricted receiver-to-source formula. Canonical embedding is known and openly credited. Residual priority risk remains, but no decisive stronger coverage was found.
residual_risks: A general regular-language subsequence transfer theorem could implicitly specialize to the stated formula without using its terminology; targeted source checks did not locate a stronger explicit covering claim.

The 2018 paper already uses unique greedy/initial embeddings in unrestricted supersequence counting; the novelty is the exact constrained q-ary spectrum and consequences, not the embedding device itself.
The accessible indexed results are ranked summaries rather than an exhaustive proof of absence, and unindexed earlier constrained-supersequence results may exist.

value.rationale: Homopolymer-free strings are an established DNA/storage source constraint, and deletions produce synchronization ambiguity. The result identifies a complete all-radius inverse-list spectrum from one local statistic, distinguishes feasible from impossible receiver words, proves a strict ambiguity hierarchy and the absence of any uniquely decodable observation for positive deletions when q>=3, and gives an exact binomial/Gaussian threshold for attainable observations. These are motivated global and asymptotic channel invariants, not a one-radius enumeration or a code-capacity assertion.
